validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED as a real line, but only via a single origin. The whole Iraq gas-operating roster (P1841/P1842/P4068/etc.) is transcribed from OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members' table (ASB 2016 Table 8.9 p.113-114; ASB 2017 Table 9.9). That table lists, under Iraq gas: 'Baiji/Al-Mashriq | OPC | 131 | 18' (columns are Connection from/to | Owner or operator | Length in MILES | Diameter in inches). Two editions (2016 & 2017) carry the identical row, so it is reproducible and authoritative, but it is one origin (OPEC), not two independent origins -> tier medium. No independent (non-OPEC, non-GEM) source I could find names this specific internal Baiji gas line. THE SHEET'S OWN SOURCES DON'T SUPPORT IT: (a) the wiki's ONLY outbound citation is 'OPEC ASB 2012 p.75', and that exact URL (opec.org/.../publications/ASB2012.pdf) now returns OPEC's HTML site shell, not the PDF (dead link, fails url_verifier). (b) The URUK / Jafar Dhia Jafar PDF cited on Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Diameter does NOT mention Baiji, Al-Mashriq/Mushraq, 211, or an 18in/160 line anywhere in its text layer (verified via pdftotext of all 8 pages) -- it only discusses North/South gas balance, Taji-Duara, and the Eastern 48in/350 line. The worklist's 'expected content present' pass on Capacity was a false positive ('160' is a substring of '16000 MW'). So that ref is irrelevant to this row and should be replaced. SPEC: Length 211 km = 131 miles x 1.609 -> OPEC's 131 mi rounds to 211 km, so GEM's 211 km is the CORRECT conversion (same miles->km pattern verified on sibling P1841: OPEC 'Baiji/Al-Qaiem 268 mi' = 431 km = GEM). Diameter 18 in = OPEC 18 in. CONFIRMED. Capacity 160 MMcf/d is UNSUPPORTED: OPEC's table has no capacity column and no other source states it; leave as-is but flag. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk -- it sits in OPEC's natural-gas pipelines table, operator OPC; not an oil/NGL line, not gathering. No concern. DUPLICATE: none. It is distinct from the separate OPEC row 'Mishraq cross road/Mousil PWR St | OPC | 38 mi | 12 in' (= GEM P4068) and from 'Baiji/Al-Qaiem' (= P1841). GEM's spelling 'Al Mushraq' conflates it with the Mishraq sulphur area near Mosul; OPEC's name is 'Al-Mashriq' (distinct token). ATTRIBUTION: OPEC gives owner/operator = OPC (Oil Pipelines Company), a Ministry of Oil subsidiary; GEM's Owner1 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is defensible at the parent level but the specific operator is OPC. FuelSource 'Bajii' is a typo for Baiji and is consistent with the Baiji origin. Start province Saladin (Salah ad-Din) is correct (Baiji is in Salah ad-Din). END endpoint 'Al-Mashriq'/Mosul could not be independently geolocated (see routes).

routes.corridor_desc: Baiji sits on the Tigris in northern Salah ad-Din (~34.929N, 43.487E). A 211 km (131 mi) gas trunk from Baiji toward the Mosul/Nineveh area would run north-northwest up the Tigris valley (roughly past Al-Shirqat ~35.46N/43.26E, Qayyarah ~35.79N/43.29E and Hammam al-Alil ~36.15N/43.26E) into greater Mosul (~36.34N/43.13E). Baiji-to-Mosul straight-line is ~155 km, so a 211 km routed length is consistent with reaching the Mosul area. This corridor is INFERRED from the endpoints + length, not from a sourced alignment; the named intermediate towns are illustrative of the valley corridor, not confirmed on-route points. The terminus 'Al-Mashriq' could not be independently geolocated, so the end coordinate is left null (no fabrication). Tightest defensible bound: Salah ad-Din -> Nineveh, following the Tigris valley.
routes.researcher_notes: Start endpoint (Baiji) and its Salah ad-Din location are well established (Wikipedia Baiji, Iraq confirms the city and governorate; coordinates ~34.929N, 43.487E). Start-vs-end pair 'Baiji/Al-Mashriq' is from OPEC ASB Table 8.9/9.9. The end node 'Al-Mashriq' is NOT confirmed geographically -- GEM's Mosul/Nineveh placement is plausible on length grounds but unsourced, and must not be conflated with the Mishraq sulphur complex (OPEC's distinct 'Mishraq cross road/Mousil' row). Coordinates for the terminus and intermediate points were deliberately NOT fabricated; corridor left as a loose Salah ad-Din -> Nineveh Tigris-valley bound. Suggested accuracy stays low.

summary: P1842 Baiji-Al Mushraq real (OPEC ASB gas table 'Baiji/Al-Mashriq', op OPC), correctly gas/transmission, no duplicate; length 211km=131mi & dia 18in CONFIRMED, but capacity 160 MMcf/d unsupported, cited URUK ref is irrelevant to this row, and 'Al-Mashriq'/Mosul terminus is unconfirmed -> confirmed (caveat).
